senses.text: alphabetical letter The twenty-first letter of the alphabet: called qaAfN . Respecting its pronunciation as the title of the fiftieth chapter of the Kur-án, see SAd , in art. Swd . It is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; its place of utterance is between the root of the tongue and the uvula, in the furthest part of the mouth; and it is of the strongest of the letters, and of the most certain of them in sound. (TA at the commencement of bAb AlqAf .) It is sometimes pronounced like the Pers. G , i. e. (L.) ― -b2- [Hence,] qadaHa fiyhi , (Msb, K,) or fiY EiroDihi , and fiY saAqihi , (A,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, (Msb,) from the incidency of the qawaAdiH [or canker-worms] in the saAq [or stem] of the tree, (A,) (tropical:) He impaired, injured, detracted from, impugned, or attacked, his honour, or reputation; blamed, censured, or reproached, him; found fault with him

; or spoke against him. (A, Msb, K.) And qadaHa fiY nasabihi (tropical:) He found fault with, or spoke against, his parentage, genealogy, or pedigree. (S, A, Msb.) And qadaHa fiY EadaAlatihi (assumed tropical:) He impugned his rectitude as a witness, mentioning something that should have the effect of causing his testimony to be rejected. (Msb.) And qadaHa fiY saAqi A^axiyhi (tropical:) He acted dishonestly, or insincerely, towards his brother, and did that which was displeasing to him, or that which he hated. (L, TA.) And fulaAnN yafut~u fiY EaDudi fulaAnK wayaqodaHu fiY saAqihi (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one seeks to injure such a one by diminishing, or impairing, ( in number or power ) the people of his house, or his aiders, or assistants; and blames, censures, or reproaches, him ]: b

2 see above, last explanation. -A2- qd~H farasahu , (S,) inf. n. taqodiyHN , (K,) (tropical:) He made his horse lean, lank, or slender: (S, K, * TA:) or qad~aHotu xayoliY , inf. n. as above, (tropical:) I made my horses to be [ like the arrows termed ] qidaAH in slenderness. (A.)

3 is (tropical:) syn. with muqaAdaEapN , [so in a copy of the A, an evident mistranscription for muqaA*aEapN , with * ,] from AlqadoHu meaning “ the act of blaming, censuring, ” &c., syn. AlT~aEonu : thus in the saying, jarato bayonahumaA muqaAdaHapN (tropical:) [ A mutual reviling, and vying in foul, or unseemly, speech or language, occurred between them two ]. (A.) ― -b2- And qAdHhu signifies (tropical:) naAZarahu [app. as meaning jaAdalahu i. e. (tropical:) He contended in an altercation, or disputed, or litigated, with him: &c.]. (A.)
5 in art. qrH .
6 (tropical:) [app. They contended in an altercation, or disputed, or litigated, each with the other ]. (A: there immediately following qaAdaHahu as meaning naAZarahu .)
7 Fire was, or became, struck, or produced, from the wood, or stick. (L in art. Sld .)

8 see 1, latter half, in three places. ― -b2- AqtdH bizanodihi is [also] a tropical phrase [meaning (tropical:) He endeavoured to avail himself of his (another's) instrumentality: or he availed himself thereof: see the phrase A^anaA muqotadiHN bizanodika in art. znd ]. (A.) ― -b3- And AqtdH AlA^amora means (tropical:) He considered, and looked into, the affair, seeking to elicit what would be its issue, or result. (A, K, TA.) ― -b4- See also 1, again; last quarter.

10 [lit. signifies He asked, or demanded, that his (another's) zinaAd (pl. of zanodN q. v.) should produce fire: and] is a tropical phrase [meaning (tropical:) He asked, or demanded, that he might avail himself of his (another's) instrumentality ]. (A.)

and ↓ , [the former, in the CK, in this case, erroneously, with fet-h to the d ,] A canker, or corrosion, incident in trees and in teeth: (L, K:) [the former is originally an inf. n.: and] each, in the sense here expl., an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates: (L:) [they are therefore more properly to be expl. as meaning a thing that cankers, or corrodes: and ↓ the latter signifies also rottenness, decay, corruption, or unsoundness: (L:) and blackness that appears in the teeth: (S:) and a crack, or fissure, in wood, or in a stick, or rod; (S, L, K;) and so the former word. (K.) ― -b2- A_borapu AlqadoHi : see miqodaHN .

An arrow, (S, Msb, K, &c.,) [i. e.] the pared wood, or rod, of an arrow, (Mgh,) before it has been furnished with feathers and a head: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.:) or an arrow when straightened, and fit to be feathered and headed: (T, voce bariY~N , q. v.:) or a rod that has attained the desired state of growth, and been pruned, and cut according to the required length for an arrow: (AHn:) and [particularly] such as is used in the game called Almayosir : (S, L:) pl. qidaAHN , (S, A, Mgh, L, K,) a pl. of mult., (TA,) and [of pauc., and accord. to the L of qidoHN in the last of the senses expl. above,] A^aqoduHu (S, L, K) and A^aqodaAHN (L, TA) and A^aqaAdiyHu , (S, L, K,) which last is a pl. pl. [i. e. pl. of A^aqodaAHN ]. (L.) [One says, in speaking of the arrows used in the game called Daraba b

[ A drinking-cup or bowl; ] a certain vessel (Msb, K) for drinking, (S, Mgh,) well known, (Msb,) large enough to satisfy the thirst of two men: (A 'Obeyd, K:) or a small one and a large one: (K:) [in the K voce EulobapN , it is applied to a vessel used for milking, sometimes made of camel's skin and sometimes of wood: it was used for drinking and for milking: ] pl. A^aqodaAHN . (S, Mgh, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad., laA tajoEaluwniY kaqadaHi Alr~akibi [ Make not ye me to be like the drinkingcup of the rider on a camel ]; meaning, make not ye me to be last in being mentioned; because the rider on a camel suspends his qdH on the hinder part of his saddle when he is finishing the puttingon of his apparatus, (Mgh, TA,) placing it behind him. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A certain measure of capacity, i

A single act of striking, or producing, fire. (IAth, K, TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (tropical:) An elicitation, by examination, of the real state or nature of a case or an affair. (IAth, TA.) ― -b3- And A single act of lading out broth [&c. with a ladle ]. (L, in so in the CK.) ― -b4- See also what next follows.
A ladleful of broth: (S, L, K:) and some say that ↓ signifies the same. (L.) You say, A^aEoTiniY qudoHapF mino maraqatika Give thou to me a ladleful of thy broth. (S.)

The act of striking or producing, fire (IAth, K, TA) with the miqodaHapN . (IAth, TA.) Hence the saying, lawo $aA='a A@ll~`hu lajaEala liln~aAsi qidoHapa ZulomapK kamaA jaEala lahumo qidoHapa nuwrK [ If God had willed, He had assigned to men the faculty of producing darkness, like as He has assigned to them the faculty of producing light ]: (K, TA:) a trad. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence] (assumed tropical:) Consideration and examination of an affair, to elicit what may be its issue, or result. (K, TA.)

and ↓ , (K,) or ↓ , (A,) (tropical:) The *ubaAb [i. e. common fly, or flies ]: (A, K, TA:) which one never sees otherwise than as though producing fire with the two fore legs [by rubbing them together like as one rubs together the zanod and the zanodap ]. (TA. [But in a verse cited by Meyd in his Proverbs, instead of AlqdwH ↓ , we find AlqaduwH AlA^aqoraH ; and he says that AlA^aqoraHu (q. v.) is from AlquroHapu , and that every *ubaAb has upon its face a quroHap (or white mark): see that verse in Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 48: and see also EM, p.

228.]) -A2- qaduwHN also signifies A well ( rakiY~N ) of which the water is laded out with the hand: (S, K:) or a well ( biy^orN ) of which the water is not taken otherwise than by successive ladings [ with the hand ]. (A.)
The pieces of wood of the [ camel's saddle called ] raHol [for which the TA has rml , but the right reading is shown by the context]: a word having no singular. (TA.)

Broth: (K: [app. because laded out:]) or some broth remaining in the bottom of the cooking-pot: (A:) or what remains in the bottom of the cooking-pot and is laded out with pains; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ . (L.)
The art, or craft, of making vessels such as are called A^aqodaAH [pl. of qadaHN ]. (K.)

: see 1, latter half: ― -b2- and see qad~aAHapN . As an epithet applied to a zanod [q. v.], (K in art. xwr ,) it signifies That produces much fire. (TK in that art.) ― -b3- See also miqodaHN . -A2- Also A maker of vessels such as are called A^aqodaAH [pl. of qadaHN ]. (K.) -A3- And a subst. signifying The blossoms of plants before they open: (TA:) or the extremities of fresh, juicy, plants: (K:) or the extremities, consisting of fresh, juicy, leaves, of plants: (TA:) or soft, or tender, suckers or offsets, of [ the species of trefoil, or clover, called ] fiSofiSap : (Az, K, TA:) of the dial. of El-'Irák: n. un. ↓ . (TA.)
A stone from which one strikes fire; (As, S, A, K;) and so ↓ . (T, S, K.) -A2- See also qad~aAHN , last sentence.

: see qaAdiHapN : ― -b2- and see also qadoHN , in two places. ― -b3- h`*aA maA='N laA yanaAmu qaAdiHuhu [ This is water of which the lader-out will not sleep ] is said in describing such [water] as is little in quantity. (A, TA.)

[ A canker-worm; ] the worm (Lth, S, Mgh, L, K) that cankers, or corrodes, trees and teeth: (Lth, * Mgh, * L, TA:) [coll. gen. n. ↓ ; occurring in the K in art. xrb , &c.:] pl. qawaAdiHu . (L.) One says, qado A^asoraEato fiY A^asonaAnihi AlqawaAdiHi [ The canker-worms have quickly come into his teeth ]. (L.)
: see qaduwHN , in three places.
: see 1, in the middle of the paragraph.

[ A couching-needle; called thus, and ↓ , in the present day. ― -b2- Also], (K, and so in some copies of the S,) and ↓ , (A, TA, and so in other copies of the S,) and ↓ , and ↓ , (K,) The thing (S, A, K) of iron (A, K) with which one strikes fire. (S, A, K.) ― -b3- And the first, A ladle; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ . (A.) ↓ [ The ladle will bring to thee what is in the bottom thereof ] is a prov., meaning, that to which thou art blind will become apparent, or manifest, to thee. (A.)
: see the next preceding paragraph, in three places.
(tropical:) Horses that are lean, lank, or slender; as though made slender [ like the arrows termed qidaAH : see 2]. (TA.)

(assumed tropical:) An eye that is sunk or depressed [ so as to be like the qadaH : see 1, last signification]. (TA.) And xabolN muqad~iHapN (assumed tropical:) Horses whose eyes are sunk or depressed. (TA.)
: see miqodaHN .
, applied to broth: see qadiyHN .

Trees having soft, weak, branches, which, when the wind puts them in motion, blaze forth with fire; but which when used for producing fire for a useful purpose, yield no fire at all: whence one says to him who has no ground of pretension to respect or honour, nor parentage, genealogy, or pedigree, of a sound quality, zanodaAka lilomutaqaAdiHi (assumed tropical:) [lit. Thy two pieces of stick, or wood, for producing fire pertain to the trees that have soft and weak branches, &c.]. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. and , [or the former only accord. to the Mgh., as will be seen by what follows,] inf. n. qadorN , (S, Msb,) is from Alt~aqodiyru , (S,) [or] it signifies the same as ↓ Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. taqodiyrN : (Msb:) [which latter phrase is afterwards mentioned in the S, but unexplained: the meaning is, I measured the thing; computed, or determined, its quantity, measure, size, bulk, proportion, extent, amount, sum, limit or limits, or number: ] Al$~aYo'a ↓ signifies he computed, or determined, or computed by conjecture, the quantity, measure, size, bulk, proportion, extent, amount, sum, or number, of the thing, ( Hazarahu ,) in order that he might know how much it was. (IKtt.) It is said in a trad., A_i*aA gum~a Ealayokumu AlhilaAlu faA@qodiruwA lahu , and faA@qoduruwA ; (S, Msb; *) or A_i

Hence, app., the saying,] A^uqoduro bi*aroEika bayonanaA See thou and know thy rank, or estimation, among us. (AO.) ― -b3- Hence also,] maA qadaruwA A@ll~`ha Haq~a qadorihi [Kur., vi. 91, and other places, meaning, And they have not estimated God with the estimation that is due to Him: or] and they have not magnified, or honoured, God, with the magnifying, or honouring, that is due to Him: (S, K:) for qadorN signifies [also] a magnifying, or honouring: (K:) or have not assigned to God the attributes that are due to Him: (Lth:) or have not known what God is in reality. (El-Basáïr.) ― -b4- qadara Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i , aor. [ and] , (L,) inf. n. qadorN ; (L, K;) and bh ↓ ; (L;) He measured the thing by the thing: (L, K: *) and EalaY mivaAlihi ↓ he measured it by its measure: (S, K, art. qys

Hence, app.,] qadara AlA^amora , (L, K,) and A_ilaY AlA^amori , (L,) aor. (L, K,) and , (L,) inf. n. qadorN ; (L, K;) [and ↓ ;] He thought upon the thing, or affair, (L,) and considered its end, issue, or result, (L, K,) and measured, or compared, one part of it with another; (L;) he measured it, compared one part of it with another, considered it, and thought upon it. (L.) See also

2. ― -b6- qadarotu Ealayohi Alv~awoba , (S, K, *) inf. n. qadorN , (S,) I made the garment according to his measure; adapted it to his measure: (S, K: *) [and qadarotu Ealayohi Al$~aYo'a app. signifies I made the thing according to his, or its, measure; proportioned, or adapted, the thing to him, or it; for wSfth , by which it is explained in the TA, seems to be, as IbrD thinks, a mistake for waDaEotuhu :] and Al$~aYo'a ↓ signifies, in like manner, he made the thing by measure, or according to a measure
; or proportioned it; syn. jaEalahu biqadarK : (IKtt:) the primary meaning of ↓ is the making a thing according to the measure of another thing. (Bd- xv.

60.) ― -b7- [Hence,] qadara A@ll~`hu *`lika Ealayohi , aor. and , inf. n. qadorN and qadarN , (K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Lh, Msb,) and maqodarapN ; (S [unless this be a simple subst.];) and Elyh ↓ , (K,) [which is more common,] inf. n. taqodiyrN ; (TA;) and lahu ; (K;) [ God decreed, appointed, ordained, or decided, that against him; and for him, or to him; accord. to an explanation of qadarN in the K: or decreed, &c., that against him; and for him, or to him; adapting it to his particular case; accord. to an explanation of qadarN by Lth, and of qadorN and qadarN in the S, and of qadarN in the Msb: see qadorN , below.] You say also qadara A@ll~`hu lahu bixayorK [ God decreed, &c., for him, good ]. (K.) ― -b8-

Also, qadara , (K,) aor. and , inf. n. qadorN , (TA,) He [ God ] distributed, divided, or apportioned, [ as though by measure, ] sustenance, or the means of subsistence. (K, TA. In the CK, the verb is qad~ara .)
Hence, say some, the appellation of layolapu Alqadori , [in the Kur, ch. xcvii.,) as being The night wherein the means of subsistence are apportioned. (TA.) See also qadorN , below. ― -b9-

Also, aor. and , but the former is that which is adopted by the seven readers [of the Kur-án], and is the more chaste, (Msb,) He (God) straitened, or rendered scanty, [ as though He measured and limited, ] the means of subsistence: (Bd, xiii. 26, and other places; and Msb:) and qudira Ealayohi rizoquhu , [see Kur, lxv. 7,] inf. n. qadorN , his means of subsistence were straitened to him; like qutira . (S, TA.) You say qadaru Ealayohi Al$~aYo'a , aor. and , (Lh, TA,) inf. n. qadorN (K,) and qadarN and qudorapN ; (Lh, TA;) and ↓ , inf. n. taqodiyrN ; (K;) He rendered the thing strait, or distressing, to him. (Lh, K, * TA.) And qadara EalaY EiyaAlihi He scanted his household

; or was niggardly or parsimonious towards them, in expenditure; like qatara . (S.) It is said in the Kur, [xxi. 87,] faZan~a A^ano lano naqodira Ealayohi And he thought that we would not straiten him: (Fr, AHeyth:) or the meaning is, lano nuqad~ira Ealayohi maA qad~aronaA mino kawonihi fiY baToni AlHuwti , for naqodir is syn. with nuqad~ir ; (Zj;) and this is correct; i. e., we would not decree against him what we decreed, of the straitness [ that should befall him ] in the belly of the fish: it cannot be from Alqudorapu [meaning power, or ability]; for he who thinks this is an unbeliever. (Az, TA.) ― -b10-

2 , inf. n. taqodiyrN : see 1, in most of its senses. ― -b2- He meditated, considered, or exercised thought in arranging and preparing, a thing or an affair; (T, K, * El-Basáïr;) either making use of his reason, and building thereon; the doing of which is praiseworthy
; or according to his desire or appetite; as in the Kur, lxxiv.

18 and 19; the doing of which is blameable; (ElBasáïr;) or by means of marks, whereby to cut it. (T.) ― -b3- He intended a thing or an affair; he determined upon it. (T.) [Said of God, He decreed, appointed, ordained, destined, predestined, or predetermined a thing.] ― -b4- [

Hence, app., qd~r ka*aA , in grammar, He meant, or held, or made, such a thing to be supplied, or understood. You say taqodiyruhu ka*aA Its (a phrase's) implied, or virtual, meaning, or meaning by implication, is thus. And yuqad~aru bika*aA Its implied meaning is to be expressed by saying thus. And taqodiyrFA is said in the sense of implicatively, or virtually, as opposed to lafoZFA or literally. ― -b5- And He supposed such a thing. ] ― -b6- He made; syn. jaEala and SanaEa . Ex., in the Kur, [xli. 9,] waqad~ara fiyhaA A^aqowaAtahaA And He made therein its foods, or aliments. And it is said in the Kur, [x. 5,] waqad~arahu manaAzila And hath made for it [the moon] mansions. (TA.) ― -b7- He knew. So in the Kur, xv. 60; and lxxiii. 20, according to the Basáïr. (TA.) -A2- qd~rhu , inf. n. taqod

1. ― -b2- qaAdarotuhu , (K,) inf. n. muqaAdarapN , (TA,) I measured myself, or my abilities, with him, or his, ( qaAyasotuhu ,) and did as he did: (K:) or I vied, or contended, with him in power, or strength. (A, TA.)

7. ― -b2- kaAna yataqad~aru fiY maraDihi A^ayona A^anaA Alyawoma [ He (Mohammad) used to compute, or reckon, in his mind, in his disease, Where am I to-day? ] i. e., he used to compute, or reckon, ( yuqad~iru ,) [in his disease,] the days of his wives, when it was his turn to visit each of them. (TA, from a trad.) See also
1. ― -b3- tqd~r It (a thing, S,) became prepared, (S, K,) lahu for him. (S.)
7 (S, K) and ↓ (A) It (a garment) agreed with, or was according to, the measure (S, A, K.) You say tqd~r Alv~awobu Ealayohi The garment agreed with, or was according to, his measure. (A.)

8 He made it of middling size; expl. by jaEalahu qadorFA . (JK, TA. [In the latter, the explanation is without any syll. signs; but in the former I find it fully pointed, and immediately followed by $aYo'N muqotadarN , thus pointed, and explained as signifying “ a thing of middling size, whether in length or tallness or in width or breadth. ”]) -A2- See also 1, last two significations.

10 He begged God to decree, appoint, ordain, or decide, for him good. (S, K.) -A2- A^al~`hum~a A_in~iY A^asotaqodiruka biqudoratika O God, I beg Thee to give me power to do it, by Thy power. (TA, from a trad.)

The quantity, quantum, measure, magnitude, size, bulk, proportion, extent, space, amount, sum, or number attained, of a thing; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ (Msb, K) and ↓ (Fr, Sgh, K) and ↓ . (Msb, K.) You say h`*aA qadoru h`*aA , and ↓ , This is the like of this [ in quantity, &c.; is commensurate with, or proportionate to, this; and so h*A ↓ ]. (Msb.) And humo qadoru miAy^pK , and mAy^p ↓ , They are as many as a hundred. (Z, Msb.) And A^axa*a biqadori Haq~ihi , and ↓ , and ↓ , He took as much as his due, or right. And qaraA^a biqadori AlfaAtiHapi , and ↓ , and ↓ , He read as much as the Fátihah. (Msb.) And A^aqamotu Einodahu qadora A^ano yafoEala ka*aA I remained at his abode long enough for him to do thus. (Meyd, TA.) But you say ↓ , thus only, with fet-h [to the dál, as is shown by what prec

Hence, Estimation, value, worth, account, rank, quality, or degree of dignity; ] greatness, majesty, honourableness, nobleness; (Msb, * TA;) gravity of character; (Msb;) as also ↓ . (Msb.) You say maA lahu EinodiY qadorN , and ↓ , He has no honourableness, or gravity of character, in my opinion. (Msb.) In the words of the Kur, [vi. 91,] wamaA qadaruwA A@ll~`ha Haq~a qadorihi , [for explanations of which see 1,] we may also correctly read ↓ . (TA.) -A2- qadorN and ↓ , (S,) [the latter of which is the more common,] or qadarN (JK, Msb, K) alone, (Msb,) or both, and ↓ and ↓ , (TA,) and ↓ , with fet-h only [to the d ], (S,) Decree, appointment, ordinance, or destiny: or what is decreed, appointed, &c.: syn. qaDaA='N and HukomN : (M, K:) or decree, &c., adapted [ to a particular case ], (Lth, JK
; or particular predestination: thus AlqaDaA='u waAlqadaru may be rendered the general and particular decrees of God

; or general and particular predestination or fate and destiny. The term qadarN is variously explained by different schools and sects: but its proper meaning seems to be that given above on the authority of Lth.] The pl. of ↓ is A^aqodaArN ; (K, TA;) and of ↓ . (TA.) You say AlA^umuwru tajoriY biqadari A@ll~`hi , and ↓ , &c., Events have their course by the decree, &c., of God. (TA.) It is said that layolapu Alqadori signifies The night of decree, &c. (TA. 1.) -A3- qadorN (A, L, K) and ↓ (L) A camel's or horse's saddle of middling size; (A, L, K;) and in like manner ↓ , applied to a horse's saddle, between small and large

; or this last signifies easy, that does not wound; like qaAtirN : (T, TA:) and ↓ , (JK,) or ↓ , (K, but see 8,) a thing, (JK,) or anything, (M, K,) of middling size, (JK, M, K,) whether in length or tallness or in width or breadth: (JK:) mqtdru Alxaloqi signifying a man, and a mountain-goat, and an antelope, of middling make: (M, TA:) and mqtdru AlTuwli a man of middling stature or tallness; (A, TA;) as also ↓ . (K.) And A^u*unN qadoraA='u An ear neither small nor large. (Sgh, K.) -A4- See also qudorapN .
A cooking-pot; a vessel in which one cooks: (Msb:) [and it very often means the food contained therein; i. e. pottage of any kind: (see, for an ex.,

senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. qurobN (S, Mgh, O, Msb *) and qurobapN and qaraAbapN and qurobaY (Mgh, Msb) and maqorabapN , (Mgh,) [to which may be added some other syns. mentioned below with qurobN and qaraAbapN ,] It, and he, was, or became, near; (S, Mgh, O;) syn. danaA ; (S, O;) contr. of baEuda : (Mgh:) or qurobN is in place, and qurobapN is in station, or grade, or rank, and qaraAbapN and qurobaY are in Alr~aHim [meaning relationship, or relationship by the female side ]; (Mgh, Msb, TA;) or, accord. to the T, qaraAbapN is in Aln~asab [app. relationship in a general sense ], and qurobaY is in Alr~aHim [app. as meaning relationship by the female side ]: (TA:) You say, qaruba minohu , (A, MA, Msb, K,) and A_ilayohi ; (A;) and qaribahu , (S, MA, O, K,) aor. ; (S, K;) inf. n. (of the former verb, Msb

; or I was, or became, near, or I approached, to it, or to doing it [or to doing something with it or to it ]: an ex. of the former meaning is the saying [in the Kur xvii. 34], laA taqorabuwA A@lz~inaA [ Commit not ye fornication, or adultery

; or, accord. to some, this is an ex. of the latter meaning]; and hence one says, qaribotu AlmaroA^apa , inf. n. qirobaAnN , a metonymical phrase, meaning I compressed the woman: and an ex. of the latter meaning is the saying, laA taqorabuwA AlHimaY i. e. laA tadonuwA minohu [meaning Approach not ye to doing, or to entering upon, the thing, or place, that is prohibited, or interdicted ]. (Msb.) And the Arabs say, of a man, when a thing has disquieted, or disturbed, and grieved, him, A^axa*ahu maA qaruba wamaA baEuda , as though meaning (assumed tropical:) He became, or has become, disquieted by reason of near and remote circumstances of his case: (O:) or recent and old griefs took hold upon him. (Mgh in art. qdm . [See art. bEd .]) danaA min~iY waqaruba is expl. by Zj as meaning He drew ne

5 in that art.) [And several other verbs belonging to this art. are syn., or nearly so, with qaruba or with qariba in senses expl. above. Thus ↓ is syn. with qaruba in the first of the senses expl. above, like as A^adonaY is with danaA , for its inf. n.] AlA_iqoraAbu signifies Ald~ubuw~u . (TA.) ↓ , also, is syn. with qaruba in the first of the senses expl. above; (MA;) [i. e.] it is syn. with danaA : (Msb:) or it is syn. with ↓ , (S, O, K, TA,) signifying he, or it, drew near; (TA;) thus ↓ AlwaEodu [in the Kur xxi. 97] signifies tqArb [meaning And the fulfilment of the promise shall draw near ]: (S, O, TA:) and you say, Aqtrb min~iY [meaning He drew near to me ]: (A:) it is also said that is has a more particular signification than qaruba ; for it denotes intensiveness in Alqurob ; thus s

Hence, also,] one says qado qaraba A^amorFA laA A^adoriY maA huwa (tropical:) [ He has sought to accomplish an affair, I know not what it is ]: (A, O: *) and fulaAnN yaqorubu A^amorFA laA yasohulu lahu (tropical:) [ Such a one seeks to accomplish an affair that will not be easy to him ]. (A.) fulaAnN yaqorubu A^amorFA means (assumed tropical:) Such a one seeks, desires, or aims at, [ the accomplishment of ] an affair, when he does a deed, or says a saying, with that object. (T, O, TA.) -A3- qaraba Als~ayofa , (S, O,) inf. n. qarobN ; (K;) and ↓ , (O,) inf. n. A_iqoraAbN ; (K;) He put the sword into the qiraAb [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) or the former, (accord. to the K,) or ↓ the latter, (accord. to the S and TA,) he made for the sword a qiraAb : (S, K, TA:) or ↓ the latter has both of these signi

2 , inf. n. taqoriybN , He made, or caused, to be, or become, near, caused to approach, or brought, or drew, near, him, or it. (S, O, Msb. *) [Hence the phrase qar~aba A@ll~`hu daAraka , which see in what follows.] ― -b2- [And hence, He made him to be a near associate; he made him an object of, or took him into, favour: and (agreeably with an explanation of the pass. in the Ham p. 184) he made him, or rendered him, an object of honour. ] One says, qar~abahu minohu meaning He (a king, or a governor, or prince, [or any other person who was either a superioror an equal,]) made him to be to him a qurobaAn , i. e. [a near associate, or] a consessor, or a particular, or special, associate or companion [&c.: see qurobaAnN ]. (TA.) ― -b3- qar~abahu A_ilayohimo , in the Kur li. 27, means He present

124.) Thus what is termed taSogiyru Alt~aqoriybi [ The diminutive denoting nearness ] is such as occurs in the saying, daAriY qubayola Almasojidi [“ My house is a little before the mosque ”]. (Kull p.

124.) ― -b6- And The advancing an argument in such a manner as renders the desired conclusion a necessary consequence. (MF.) ― -b7- And A certain sort of Eadow [or running ] (S, O, K) of a horse: (S, O:) one says, of a horse, qr~b , inf. n. taqoriybN , (S, A, O,) meaning he raised his fore legs together and put them down together (S, O, K *) in running: (S, O:) or he ran [ as though ] pelting the ground [ with his hoofs ]: (AZ, TA:) and it is also said of other animals than the horse: but not of the camel: (MF:) [one sort of] Altqryb is [a rate] less than AlHuDoru ; (S, A, O;) and more than Alxababu : (El-Ámidee, MF:) there are two sorts of tqryb , called A^aEolaY [which is a gallop ] and A^adonaY [which is a canter ]: (S, O:) the former is termed Alv~aEolabiy~apu ; and the latter, AlA_iro

3 , inf. n. muqaArabapN [and qiraAbN ], I was, or became, near to him, or it; contr. of baAEadotuhu . (Msb.) See 1, near the middle of the paragraph. ― -b2- One says of a vessel, (S, O, K,) qArb A^ano yamotaliy^a (S, O) or qArb AlAimotilaA='a (K) [ It was, or became, near to being full ]: qArb [thus used] is the verb from qarobaAnu [q. v.], and qaruba is not used in its stead. (Sb, TA.) And one says also, qArb miloA^ahu [ It was, or became, nearly equal, or it nearly amounted, to what would fill it ]. (Msb.), And qArb qadorahu [ It was, or became, nearly equal, or equivalent, to its quantity, or amount

; or it was, or became, nearly equivalent to it ]. (K, TA.) [And hence the term A^afoEaAlu AlmuqaArabapi The verbs of appropinquation; as kaAda &c.] ― -b3- qArb AlxaTowa He made the stepping to be contracted; syn. daAnaAhu ; (AZ, K, TA;) [i. e. he made short steps: made his steps to be near together; ] said of a horse. (TA.) And qArb kalaAmahu [ He made the several portions of his speech, i. e. he made his words, to be near together; so that it means he uttered his speech rapidly ]. (K in art. wT ; &c.) And qArb byn Alkalimapi waAlkalimapi fiY Alt~asobiyHi [ He made the words to follow one another nearly, or to be near together, in the act of praise, or the like.] (M in art. dnw .) And qaArabotu bayona AlA^amorayoni i. q. daAnayotu [ I made the two affairs, or events, to be nearly uninterr

634.) And qArb AlA^amora He thought the thing. (MF.) ― -b5- And He interchanged with him good, or pleasing, speech. (O, K, TA.) ― -b6- And qArb fiY AlA^amori He pursued the right, or just, or middle, course, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it, in the affair. (O, * K, * TA.) ― -b7- And qaArabotuhu fiY AlbayoEi [app. meaning, in like manner, I pursued a middle course with him in selling, or buying, with respect to the price demanded or offered, neither exceeding what was just nor falling short of it ], (S, O,) inf. n. muqaArabapN . (S.) ― -b8- muqaArabapN and qiraAbN signify also The raising the leg [or legs, of a woman,] for the purpose of jimaAE . (K.)

(Lth, S, A, O, K.) ― -b3- And Aqrb said of a colt, and of a young camel, (K, TA,) &c., (TA,) He was, or became, near to the age of shedding his central incisors; (K, TA;) and likewise, to that of shedding other teeth. (TA.) ― -b4- And He nearly filled a vessel. (S, O, K.) ― -b5- laA^uqoriban~akumo SalaApa rasuwli A@ll~`hi occurs in a trad. of Aboo-Hureyreh, meaning I will indeed perform to you t

(As, O, L, K, TA.) Only the imperative mood in this sense is said to be used. (MF, TA.) ― -b3- And [hence, also,] tqr~b signifies He rendered himself near, or allied himself, [ drew near, or ingratiated himself, ] by affection and friendship. (TA, voce tanas~aba . [In this sense it is trans. by means of mino .]) And He applied himself with gentleness, or courtesy, to obtain access, or nearness, to a man, by means of some act performed for that purpose, or by right. (TA. [In this sense it is trans. by means of A_ilaY .]) And one says, tqr~b mina A@ll~`hi [ He drew near unto God

; or to advance himself in the favour of God: (S, K, * TA:) and faEalahu taqar~ubFA A_ilayohi [ He did it by way of seeking nearness, &c., to Him ]. (A.) -A2- tqr~b also signifies He (a man, O) put his hand upon his qurob (O, K, TA) i. e. his flank, (O, TA,) in walking
; or, as some say, hastening, or going quickly. (TA.)

(A.) ― -b2- See also 1, second quarter. ― -b3- tqArbt A_ibiluhu means (tropical:) His camels became few, [because drawing near together,] (A, O, K, TA,) and (as is also said of other things, TA) declined, or became reduced to a bad state. (O, * K, * TA.) ― -b4- And [for the like reason, because of its becoming dense,] tqArb is said of seed-produce, or standing corn or the like, meaning (assumed tropical:) It became nearly ripe. (O, K, TA.) ― -b5- And hence [accord. to some], taqaAraba Alz~amaAnu (assumed tropical:) [ When the time becomes contracted ], occurring in a trad., expl. in

; or admission into favour ]. (A.) ― -b2- See also qaraAbapN . ― -b3-
